To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have characterized the E11 and the E1 promoter of the mu opioid gene in transgenic mouse model.
we have established a transgenic mouse for studying the E11 and the E1 promoter in various regions of mouse brain.

the E11 promoter controls nine alternatively spliced variants in the mouse mu opioid gene and the transgenic model using tau/Lac Z and tau/GFP reporter provides a useful tool to study the E1 and E1 promoters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms of the E11 and the E1 promoter, which are important for regulating Oprm gene expression in the CNS.
the characterization of the E11 and the E1 promoters of Oprm gene in vivo using transgenic mice.
the characterization of the E11 and 1 exons promoter of the Oprm gene in transgenic mouse model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have generated a transgenetic mouse line to study E11 and E11 promoters in vivo using the tau/LacZ or tau/GFP reporter gene, and the reasonable relevance of the model was demonstrated by temporal and spatial expression as compared to those endogenous transcripts.
we have generated a transgene model to characterize the E11 promoter in vivo using tau/GFP reporter.
the E11 promoter is a functional promoter that is expressed in the CNS during embryonic development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have generated a transgene mouse line to study two promoters, E11 and E2, of the mu opioid gene in vivo using tau/lacZ and tau/green fluorescence protein (GFP) reporters.
the E11 promoter is a functional promoter that is expressed in a temporal and spatial pattern similar to that for the endogenous Oprm gene.
we have successfully established a transgenic mouse for the study of the Oprm gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transgenic model can be a useful tool to characterize gene promoters in vivo.
the E11 promoter is widely expressed in the brain, suggesting that the nine splice variants regulated by the E11 promoter are widely distributed in the brain.

the E11 promoter controls a set of splice variants in the Oprm gene that are different from those controlled by the E1 promoter, and that the E11 splice variants are differentially expressed in the CNS.
